domain_label: TOEFL Content (from zero) — CEFR Learning Ladder, Vocabulary Anchors & Resource Shelf (A1 -> university-minimum band 4 / competitive band 5)

glossary.definition: The backbone the whole ladder hangs on: the 2026 TOEFL 1-6 band scale is CEFR-aligned by design (ETS score-scale-update page, FACT) so every stage target is stated as a CEFR level first and a band second; band ~4.0 approximates B2 and ~5.0 approximates C1 as third-party estimate anchors, with band 4.5 approximately 90 on the legacy 0-120 scale the one ETS-firm point.

The common admission floor: band ~4.0 approximating CEFR B2 approximating legacy ~72+ [ESTIMATE, medium-high]. It is the default target for a from-zero learner headed to a typical university and the point at which the academic B1->B2 stage is cleared; ETS itself sets no pass mark, so this is a destination requirement, not an exam threshold.

The higher target for selective programs: band ~5.0 approximating CEFR C1 approximating legacy ~95+ [ESTIMATE, medium-high]. Reaching it is a speed-and-accuracy climb under two-stage adaptive pressure rather than new content, because the upper Reading/Listening modules surface C1/C2 items only when Stage-1 performance earns them.

The single citable vocabulary-size source used here: Milton & Alexiou (2009), an XLex first-5K-band study across 500+ learners, measuring A2 ~1,500-2,500, B1 ~2,750-3,250 and B2 ~3,250-3,750 words and finding vocabulary size explains ~60-70% of CEFR-level variance [FACT]. No vocabulary number outside this study is stated as fact.

The pass/no-pass check between ladder rungs: a stage is cleared only when its vocabulary anchor is met AND a sample-test band read holds at or above the stage's band, so the learner climbs on demonstrated proficiency, not elapsed time; there is no ETS hours-per-band figure to gate on [UNKNOWN].

The mapping that tells a learner which 2026 task types are practiseable at their current rung: R1/S1 at A1 foundation; R2, L2, L3, W2 at A2->B1 functional; R3, L4, W3, S2 at B1->B2 academic; upper-module Reading/Listening at C1 — so practice targets the rung being climbed rather than tasks still out of reach.

The prep inventory: official ETS items (TOEFL TestReady free portal, the free Jan-2026 sample test and ~40-minute familiarization, the free 2026 Blueprint & Specifications PDF, the forthcoming Official Guide for the 2026 format) and notable free third-party sets (TST Prep, Magoosh, toeflresources, TestGlider, goarno.io), the latter unaudited against the official spec [UNKNOWN quality].

The order the shelf is consumed: TestReady daily free rotating activity -> the free Jan-2026 sample test as first diagnostic -> paid TestReady section/full-length tests -> the Official Guide's practice tests as the mock spine, with free third-party material filling gaps only where its unaudited status is acceptable (drilling, not scoring).

The explicit blocker on this ladder: no ETS publication of study-hours-per-CEFR-band or hours-to-target was found, so the plan is stage/skill-gated and never quotes an hour count; likewise exact country fees and university cutoffs are out of scope as numbers because their authoritative pages were unreachable.

nodes.definition: Choose the target band from the destination's stated requirement, because the target sets the whole ladder's length and top rung. Two common targets: the university minimum, CEFR B2 approximating band ~4.0 approximating legacy ~72+ [ESTIMATE, medium-high], the default for a from-zero learner headed to a typical program; and the competitive target, CEFR C1 approximating band ~5.0 approximating legacy ~95+ [ESTIMATE, medium-high], for selective programs. nodes.definition: Turn the Milton & Alexiou anchors into a per-stage, frequency-ordered cumulative vocabulary target the ladder can gate on. Acquire highest-frequency words first: the foundation aims at ~2,000 highest-frequency words (the A2 anchor of ~1,500-2,500), the functional stage carries toward the B1 anchor ~2,750-3,250, and the academic stage reaches the B2 anchor ~3,250-3,750 that supports band 4 [all sizes FACT-sourced to Milton & Alexiou 2009]. Frequency-ordering matters because the first few thousand words cover the great majority of everyday and test text, and vocabulary size explains ~60-70% of CEFR-level variance, so it is the single most leveraged growth axis. The Nation-style ~8,000-9,000 academic word families sit ABOVE the band-4 target and are pursued only for a C1 competitive climb, and even then as a labeled estimate [ESTIMATE, medium]. No hour count is attached to the growth — it is gated by size reached, not time spent.

nodes.definition: Define the first rung, A0->A2 foundation: build the ~2,000 highest-frequency words (Milton & Alexiou A2 band ~1,500-2,500), the basic sentence patterns (SVO, yes/no and wh- questions, and the past/present/future the everyday tasks need), and phonics plus listen-and-repeat oral drilling. This is exactly the level the 2026 test reaches DOWN to: its easiest items sit at A1, so foundation work is directly on-test, not pre-test [FACT that the 2026 test measures down to A1; blueprint-derived sources]. Clearing this rung first unlocks the two most form-focused task types — R1 Complete the Words (type the deleted second half of words in a short paragraph) and S1 Listen and Repeat (hear seven sentences once, repeat each aloud) — which reward exactly the orthographic and phonological control the foundation builds.

Target band for this rung is ~3-3.5 (approximately B1) [ESTIMATE, medium]. It is the bridge rung: the learner is now answering real test tasks across three sections, so it is where practice on official everyday-life items begins in earnest.

nodes.definition: Define the third rung, B1->B2 academic, the one that reaches the university-minimum band ~4.0: build comprehension and production of ~200-word academic passages (history, sciences, social sciences, humanities; no prior knowledge assumed), ~90-second academic talks, the 10-minute Writing for an Academic Discussion post (W3: read a professor prompt plus peer posts, contribute a reasoned reply), and 45-second spontaneous interview answers (S2, no prep time), carrying vocabulary to the Milton & Alexiou B2 anchor ~3,250-3,750+ [task facts blueprint-derived; vocabulary FACT-sourced]. This rung is where reasoned argument, inference and timed spontaneous production replace everyday recall — it is the hardest single rung for most from-zero learners and the true objective for a typical university applicant. Clearing it is the university-minimum band-4 gate.

nodes.definition: Define the top rung, B2->C1 (band ~4 to ~5), for a competitive target: this climb is speed plus accuracy under two-stage adaptive pressure, NOT new content. Reading and Listening are multistage adaptive — everyone gets the same Stage 1, and Stage 2 difficulty (and item count/time) rises with Stage-1 performance — so the C1/C2-level items only surface once the learner earns them, and the rung is about answering the same task types faster and more accurately to unlock and clear the harder module [FACT that R/L are two-stage adaptive and upper modules reach C1/C2; blueprint-derived]. Vocabulary pushes past the B2 anchor toward the Nation-style academic families, carried as an estimate not a firm requirement [ESTIMATE]. Most from-zero learners headed to a typical university do NOT need this rung; it is reserved for selective-program targets.

conflict_axes.description: Only band 4.5 approximately 90 is firm, so a precise band-to-legacy equivalence invites presenting an estimate cell as an exact score to an admissions office.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: present only the ETS-firm 4.5~90 point as exact and every other conversion as a labeled estimate range

conflict_axes.name: start_at_foundation_vs_placed_entry
conflict_axes.description: Defaulting every learner to the foundation rung is safe but wastes a non-beginner's time, while trusting a rough placement risks entering too high.
poles: start everyone at the foundation rung
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: place with the free sample test plus a vocabulary-size estimate, enter at the matching rung, and re-run placement if early practice shows a mis-fit

conflict_axes.name: section_drill_vs_full_adaptive_mock
conflict_axes.description: Section drills are plentiful but cannot reproduce the two-stage adaptive behaviour, while faithful full mocks that can are scarce.
poles: read a band from section drills
read a band from a full adaptive mock
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: read every gate band from a full adaptive official mock and space the scarce mocks so each reads a gate

conflict_axes.name: single_source_vocabulary_vs_richer_but_unsourced
conflict_axes.description: Binding vocabulary numbers to the one Milton & Alexiou study is narrow, but richer round-number targets circulating online are unsourced.
poles: use a richer unsourced word-count target
stay bound to the Milton & Alexiou anchor
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: state only Milton & Alexiou sizes as fact and carry any other figure, like Nation ~8-9k, as a labeled estimate not required for band 4

conflict_axes.name: tag_dense_honesty_vs_learner_simplicity
conflict_axes.description: Dense FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tagging keeps the plan auditable but can clutter learner-facing advice, tempting tag-stripping.
poles: strip tags for a clean learner handout
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the source or estimate/unknown tag on every number even in simplified advice, or omit the number entirely

edge_cases.description: A tutor quotes an invented 'hours to B2' figure to satisfy a learner who wants a timeline
edge_cases.trigger: a demand for a concrete study-hours estimate that no ETS source supplies
edge_cases.mitigation: state that hours-per-band is unknown and answer with the stage-gate substitute (vocabulary anchor met plus band read holding), never an hour count

edge_cases.description: A vocabulary target not measured by Milton & Alexiou (a round '5,000 words for TOEFL') is stated as fact
edge_cases.trigger: a circulating unsourced word-count target is adopted
edge_cases.mitigation: state only the Milton & Alexiou A2/B1/B2 sizes as fact and mark any other figure an estimate, or drop it

edge_cases.description: An estimate band-to-legacy cell (band 4.0 'equals' exactly 72) is presented to an admissions office as an exact equivalence
edge_cases.trigger: a precise legacy point is read off an estimate conversion
edge_cases.mitigation: present only the ETS-firm band-4.5~90 point as exact and every other conversion as a labeled estimate range

edge_cases.description: A learner is aimed at C1/band-5 when the destination requires only B2/band-4
edge_cases.trigger: the target is set above the destination's actual cutoff
edge_cases.mitigation: read the target off the destination cutoff and stop at the band-4 academic gate when B2 admits the learner

edge_cases.description: A non-beginner is defaulted to the foundation rung and wastes weeks on already-known high-frequency vocabulary
edge_cases.trigger: placement is skipped and everyone starts at the foundation
edge_cases.mitigation: run the free-sample-test plus vocabulary-size placement and enter at the matching rung

edge_cases.description: A gate band read is taken from isolated section drills instead of a full adaptive mock and over-states readiness
edge_cases.trigger: a full mock is unavailable so a drill score is used as the band read
edge_cases.mitigation: read every gate band from a full adaptive official mock and space the scarce mocks to cover the gates

edge_cases.description: An unaudited third-party 'TOEFL' item still built to the legacy format is practised as current
edge_cases.trigger: a free third-party resource that has not tracked the 2026 overhaul is used
edge_cases.mitigation: check third-party items against the 2026 Blueprint and use them for drilling only, deferring to the official shelf on format

edge_cases.description: The Nation ~8,000-9,000 academic word families figure is presented as a band-4 requirement
edge_cases.trigger: an academic-reading word-family estimate is mistaken for the university-minimum target
edge_cases.mitigation: flag ~8-9k families as an estimate above the band-4 target, pursued only for a C1 competitive climb

edge_cases.description: An exact Official Guide publication date or ISBN is quoted as fact before the edition ships
edge_cases.trigger: the ~August-2026 Official Guide is cited with a precise unverified date or ISBN
edge_cases.mitigation: state the Guide's existence and ~Aug-2026 plan with the exact date and ISBN marked unknown

edge_cases.description: A learner clears the academic rung on reading alone while timed S2 speaking and W3 writing lag
edge_cases.trigger: readiness is declared on the strongest section rather than the whole rung
edge_cases.mitigation: require the target band read to hold across all four sections of a full mock before clearing the rung

edge_cases.description: The single free full practice test is burned early, leaving no fresh full mock to read a later gate
edge_cases.trigger: the scarce free full test is used before a gate needs it
edge_cases.mitigation: space the free and paid full tests so each reads a specific gate, buying paid TestReady tests when free volume runs out

edge_cases.description: A simplified learner handout strips the FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tags off the conversion and vocabulary numbers
edge_cases.trigger: advice is simplified for a learner and the provenance tags are dropped
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the source or estimate/unknown tag on every number even in simplified advice, or omit the number

workflow.action: Fix the CEFR-band spine and choose the target
workflow.description: State the CEFR-aligned 1-6 scale, the band~CEFR estimate anchors and the firm 4.5~90 point, then set the university-minimum or competitive target
workflow.gate: the target is stated as a CEFR level first, a band second and its legacy equivalent, read off the destination requirement

workflow.description: State the Milton & Alexiou A2/B1/B2 sizes and the ~60-70% variance figure as the only citable vocabulary source
workflow.gate: every vocabulary size carries the Milton & Alexiou source and no other vocabulary number is stated as fact

workflow.description: Give the B1/B2/C1/C2 legacy anchors as estimates, name the firm 4.5~90 point and the dual-reporting window
workflow.gate: every conversion cell except 4.5~90 is flagged estimate and the dual-reporting window is stated

workflow.action: Turn the anchors into a per-stage vocabulary growth plan
workflow.description: Front-load ~2,000 high-frequency words and set each rung's cumulative target to the matching anchor, size-gated not time-gated
workflow.gate: each stage target ties to a Milton & Alexiou anchor, is gated on size not hours, and reserves ~8-9k families for the C1 climb as an estimate

workflow.description: Specify foundation, functional, academic and competitive rungs with their content, vocabulary target and band
workflow.gate: each rung names its content, vocabulary anchor and CEFR/band, and the academic rung is marked the band-4 university-minimum gate

workflow.action: Peg the 2026 task types to the rungs
workflow.description: Map R1/S1, R2/L2/L3/W2/W1, R3/L4/W3/S2 and the upper modules to the rung each first becomes practiseable at
workflow.gate: the pegs are stated as estimates over the FACT A1-to-C1/C2 range and target practice to the current rung

workflow.action: Inventory and sequence the resource shelf
workflow.description: List the official shelf and the free third-party set, then order them free-first
workflow.gate: the official shelf is authoritative, the third-party set is marked unaudited, and the free-first order is stated with the Official Guide date/ISBN unknown

workflow.description: Use the free sample test as first diagnostic and space the free/paid full tests to read each gate
workflow.gate: gate band reads come from full adaptive mocks, not drills, and the scarce mocks are spaced across the gates

workflow.action: Place the learner and define the stage gates
workflow.description: Place with the sample test plus a vocabulary-size estimate, then set each gate as vocabulary anchor met plus band read holding
workflow.gate: entry is at the placed rung, each gate has objective vocabulary-plus-band-read exit criteria, and no hour quota is attached

workflow.action: Hold the honesty discipline across all numbers
workflow.description: Tag every vocabulary, conversion, resource and task number FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN and name the hours/fees/cutoffs blockers
workflow.gate: every number carries its source or estimate/unknown tag and the hours/fees/cutoffs unknowns are named not filled

workflow.action: Compose the ordered climb and the readiness verdict
workflow.description: Assemble placement->entry->gates->target with per-rung tasks, vocabulary and resources, then compose the three-condition readiness go/no-go
workflow.gate: the plan is skill-gated with tags carried and the verdict requires the target full-mock band read, the met vocabulary anchor and fully tagged numbers

dominance_rules.rule: The Milton & Alexiou source dominates any other vocabulary-size claim
dominance_rules.rationale: it is the only citable lexical-size-vs-CEFR study on this ladder, so unsourced word counts have no standing
dominance_rules.action: attach the Milton & Alexiou source or, for any other figure, a labeled estimate tag, or drop the number

dominance_rules.rule: The stage gate dominates any hours-to-target timeline
dominance_rules.rationale: no ETS study-hours-per-band figure exists, so progress can only be measured by demonstrated proficiency
dominance_rules.trigger: a timeline or hours question is asked
dominance_rules.action: answer with the stage-gate substitute (vocabulary anchor met plus band read holding) and never quote an hour count

dominance_rules.rule: The full adaptive mock dominates a section drill as the gate band read
dominance_rules.rationale: Reading and Listening are two-stage adaptive and a drill cannot reproduce the Stage-1/Stage-2 behaviour
dominance_rules.trigger: a stage gate needs a band read
dominance_rules.action: read the band from a full adaptive official mock, not from isolated section drills

dominance_rules.rule: The official shelf dominates any unaudited third-party resource on format or scoring
dominance_rules.rationale: only the official ETS shelf is authoritative on the 2026 spec; third-party material is unaudited
dominance_rules.trigger: a third-party resource conflicts with the official shelf
dominance_rules.action: defer to the official shelf and use the third-party material for drilling volume only

dominance_rules.rule: The ETS-firm 4.5~90 point dominates any other band-to-legacy conversion as exact
dominance_rules.rationale: it is the only firm interior conversion point; all other cells are estimates
dominance_rules.trigger: a band is converted to a legacy 0-120 score
dominance_rules.action: state only 4.5~90 as exact and carry every other conversion as a labeled estimate range

dominance_rules.rule: The destination requirement dominates the ambition to over-climb
dominance_rules.rationale: over-targeting C1 when B2 is required lengthens the ladder for no admission benefit
dominance_rules.trigger: a target band is chosen above the destination cutoff
dominance_rules.action: set the target to the destination's actual cutoff and climb the C1 rung only when a selective program needs it

dominance_rules.rule: The placed entry rung dominates the default-to-foundation habit
dominance_rules.rationale: a non-beginner wastes time repeating a rung they have already cleared
dominance_rules.action: place with the sample test plus vocabulary estimate and enter at the matching rung, re-running placement if mis-fit appears

dominance_rules.rule: Skill practice dominates raw vocabulary-size chasing on the academic rung
dominance_rules.rationale: vocabulary size is only ~60-70% of CEFR variance and the academic rung is reasoning and timed production
dominance_rules.trigger: academic-rung time is spent maximizing word count
dominance_rules.action: meet the B2 size as a gate floor and spend rung time on R3/L4/W3/S2 skill work

dominance_rules.rule: The provenance tag dominates learner-facing simplicity
dominance_rules.rationale: an untagged number can be mistaken for an ETS fact and mislead a high-stakes decision
dominance_rules.trigger: advice is simplified for a learner
dominance_rules.action: keep the source or estimate/unknown tag on every number, or omit the number entirely

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read the destination's actual cutoff and set the target band before building any rung
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a C1-length ladder for a learner a B2 destination would have admitted, wasting months

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the sample-test-plus-vocabulary placement before choosing the entry rung
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a non-beginner repeating the foundation rung or a beginner stalling one entered too high

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the Milton & Alexiou source (or an estimate tag) to every vocabulary number when it is first written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unsourced word-count target circulating as fact and being retracted from a learner plan later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Carry the FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tags from the research into every number from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an estimate conversion or an unknown being presented to an admissions office as an exact ETS fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the hours/fees/cutoffs unknowns and the gate substitute up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an invented hours-to-target timeline being promised and then abandoned when it slips

anti_rework_rules.rule: Space the scarce full mocks to read specific gates rather than using them early
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reaching a gate with no fresh full adaptive mock left to confirm the band read

anti_rework_rules.rule: Require the target band read to hold across all four sections before clearing a rung
anti_rework_rules.prevents: declaring readiness on a strong section while a lagging S2 or W3 fails on test day

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check any third-party resource against the 2026 Blueprint before adopting it for practice
anti_rework_rules.prevents: drilling legacy-format items that no longer match the current test and having to re-learn the format

iteration_protocol.trigger: ETS's full CEFR cell-by-cell table or a firmer band<->CEFR anchor becomes reachable
iteration_protocol.action: replace the estimate band~CEFR cutoffs with the confirmed cells and re-check the target and conversion nodes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a newer citable lexical-size-vs-CEFR study is located or the academic word-family figure is re-verified
iteration_protocol.action: update the vocabulary anchors and the per-stage growth targets and re-tag the estimate figures

iteration_protocol.trigger: the 2026 Official Guide ships and its practice tests, date and ISBN become known
iteration_protocol.action: add the Guide to the mock spine, resolve its date/ISBN unknown, and re-sequence the free-first order

iteration_protocol.trigger: the ETS Blueprint PDF becomes fetchable and confirms per-module item counts or per-task CEFR targeting
iteration_protocol.action: firm up the task-to-rung pegs and the adaptive-unlock framing and re-tag them from estimate to fact where confirmed

iteration_protocol.trigger: a learner's mock band read and vocabulary-size count repeatedly disagree at a gate
iteration_protocol.action: re-examine the gate criteria and the placement, checking for a depth-of-knowledge gap behind a met size

iteration_protocol.trigger: the transition dual-reporting window ends and destinations move to band-only cutoffs
iteration_protocol.action: retire the legacy conversion bridge from the target expression and re-check the readiness verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: a credible study-hours-per-band guideline is published or the ETS fee page becomes reachable
iteration_protocol.action: revisit the hours/fees blocker and, if a source is genuinely firm, replace the unknown with the tagged figure

priority_rationale: The CEFR-band spine, target selection and the citable vocabulary anchors come first because every rung, gate and resource choice is read against the CEFR target and the one sourced vocabulary study; the legacy bridge and the per-stage vocabulary growth plan next, because they turn the spine and anchors into destination-usable scores and gateable size targets; the four ladder rungs then apply that to the A1-to-C1 climb; the task-to-rung map, resource shelf, free-first sequencing and mock spine follow because they supply what to practise and what to practise it on, rung by rung; placement and the stage-gate protocol then make the climb a placed, objectively gated sequence; the hours-unknown and source-tagging honesty nodes govern every number throughout; and the ordered ladder plan and the readiness go/no-go come last because they compose placement, gates, tasks, resources and tags into one climb and a single demonstrated-band-plus-honest-numbers registration verdict.
